body: I think the use of integers is deliberate, sure _scaling the containers_ looks more visually pleasing here, but in practice wouldn't this introduce scaling artifacts due to subpixel positioning? Especially in pixel-perfect games.

Using floats for Controls has benefits when scaling or zooming in, being in a Container doesn't change that. All controls already support floating point position and size, it's only some Containers children that restrict it to ints. It's inconsistent which Containers use floats and which don't and even how they do it https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/76265#issuecomment-2864554404 , so I doubt it was fully intentional, but if it was it should be unified anyway. It causes issues too, like not respecting the full minimum size of the children, or graph node has https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/36522.

The reason I have left this as a draft is because there are currently issues if you do want it to snap to pixels. The pixel snapping options (`gui/common/snap_controls_to_pixels`, `rendering/2d/snap/snap_2d_transforms_to_pixel`, or `rendering/2d/snap/snap_2d_vertices_to_pixel`) only snap the positions, not the sizes of controls in my testing, which makes it look off when enabled and you scale/zoom. `snap_controls_to_pixels` is enabled by default too.
I'm not sure how to resolve it, I don't know much about these settings. We may need to modify one of them or add a new option that snaps the sizes. Or have the Container change the logic based on if its enabled or something.
Otherwise, I don't think sub-pixel positioning itself causes issues, especially with snap settings enabled. After all, Controls already use floats. I'll check again after a solution for the size issue though.

It should be possible to have both smooth UI and pixel-snapped UI.
